title: Regional access request orchestration and enterprise triage
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define an operational intake + prioritization flow for enterprise region availability and data residency requests that balances legal/regulatory constraints, latency/availability requirements, and Redwood commercial strategy.

Scope: New region onboarding requests, customer-mandated data residency (contractual residency clauses), multi-region failover requests for SLOs, and enterprise-controlled routing for Dedicated/Private deployments. This ticket produces the orchestration play (who does what when), a lightweight scoring rubric, the handoff checklist to Eng/Infra, and a sample decision letter for customers.

Out of scope: raw cloud provider procurement, long-term capacity procurement contracts, and on-prem installation engineering (handled in ENG sub-issues).
intake_signals: AE escalation (deal requires region/residency before close)
Support ticket tagged 'residency' or 'region' from enterprise customer
Legal/compliance audit report requesting regional controls
Contract clause flagged during procurement or renewal
SLO/latency alert patterns indicating customer needs for regional failover
triage_criteria: Customer business criticality (weight 35) — revenue at risk, compliance fines, go-live dates
Legal/regulatory mandate (weight 30) — explicit residency requirement by law or contract
Technical feasibility & runway (weight 15) — infra effort, model compatibility, data path complexity
Operational cost delta (weight 10) — estimated monthly cost vs hosted baseline
Strategic value (weight 10) — market expansion, referenceability, competitive leverage
scoring_example: Example: GlobalBank request for EU-residency + regional failover: Business criticality 9/10 => 31.5 points, Legal mandate 10/10 => 30 points, Feasibility 6/10 => 9 points, Cost delta 4/10 => 4 points, Strategic 7/10 => 7 points. Total = 81.5 => 'High priority: Sales-assisted path + legal exception SLA'.
proposed_flow: 1) Auto-classify inbound request via intake form and ticket tags; 2) Run automated scoring to produce priority band (Low/Medium/High/Critical); 3) If score >= 70, open 'Enterprise Intake Review' meeting with PM, Legal, Solutions Eng, and Infrastructure; 4) Produce Technical Impact Assessment (TIA) by engineering within 5 business days; 5) Commercial/Legal draft contract appendix and residency SLA; 6) If accepted, schedule Dedicated/Private onboarding epic and assign ENG owner; 7) Post-launch: 90-day monitoring with latency/cost report and playbook updates.
owners: Liam Chen — Product owner, region enablement
acceptance_criteria: A one-page orchestration playbook exists summarizing intake, scoring, and handoff
Automated intake form + ticket template (Zendesk/Linear) implemented
Scoring rubric validated on 8 historical enterprise requests (retroactive scoring)
Triage SLA: initial review scheduled within 3 business days for high/critical requests
Handoff checklist populated and used in one pilot onboarding
Decision letter templates (approve/partial/decline) committed to docs
